title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: article describes standard dictionary human resource management information system (HRMIS) data, organized three main modules: Establishment, Personnel, Contract. modules designed organize standardize information public sector personnel across different countries administrative levels.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: Establishment module captures information public sector institutions, including ministries, departments, agencies.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: Establishment Type: Indicates hierarchical level institution within government structure. Ideally, support parent-child relationships, though data may rare practice. Administration Level: Refers geographic/administrative level government (e.g., national, state/provincial, local). Reference Date: Critical tracking establishmental changes, mergers, renaming time.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: Personnel module contains demographic employment information individual public sector employees.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: Education Categories: Multiple classification systems provided allow cross-country comparisons mapping international standards. Geographic Information: personnels linked establishments, separate geographic fields allow tracking mobility remote work arrangements. Privacy Considerations: module contains sensitive personal information handled according applicable data protection regulations.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: Contract module captures details employment contracts, compensation, job characteristics.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: Compensation Fields: Multiple salary measures allow analysis gross--net ratios, taxation effects, allowances. Occupation Coding: native standardized (ISCO) classifications enable within-country detail cross-country comparability. Contract Duration: combination contract_type, start_date, end_date provides comprehensive information employment stability temporary arrangements.

title: HR Standard Data Dictionary
text: three modules related follows: One establishment can many personnels One establishment can many contracts One personnel can multiple contracts (time concurrent)
code: Establishment (1) ←→ (N) Personnel Establishment (1) ←→ (N) Contract Personnel (1) ←→ (N) Contract

text: Temporal Consistency: Ensure ref_date fields properly maintained across modules Geographic Consistency: Country administration codes consistent across modules Unique Identifiers: ID fields globally unique persistent Missing Data: Document conventions handling missing unavailable data Historical Records: Consider versioning strategy tracking changes time

title: HR Data Harmonization
text: Contract Module foundational component harmonized payroll dataset. purpose module extract structure information unique contract, reference date level, defined data dictionary. “contract record” refers personnel–contract relationship specific reference period (usually month–year), capturing contractual characteristics governing personnel’s employment time. practice, raw HRMIS data typically mixes variables different conceptual levels—personnel attributes, position attributes, contract terms, payroll events, sometimes even one-administrative transactions. Working payroll HRMIS data many developing-country contexts often involves large datasets—sometimes millions records spanning multiple years. data volumes can quickly overwhelm standard analytical workflows handled using efficient tools. R, several paradigms manipulating two-dimensional data. purposes tutorial, rely data.table package tasks computationally intensive. time writing, data.table remains gold standard high-performance data processing R, offering exceptional speed, efficient memory use, expressive syntax tailored large datasets. Although dplyr package tidyverse ecosystem widely used favored readability intuitive grammar, operations large payroll datasets can substantially slower using dplyr alone. ensure reproducibility, performance, scalability—especially teams limited computational resources—adopt data.table primary engine harmonization. However, also use dplyr functions performance improved ensure code readability. bra_hrmis data written Portuguese might require translation English ease understanding. One option use LLM like ChatGPT get quick 34 columns. Alternatively polyglotr R package provides suite functions support translation. can applied follows: first step handling raw payroll dataset find individual identifies countract time period unique. begin looking bra_hrmis object . table previous glimpse(), can see CPF MATRICULA variables likely candidates identify contracts uniquely. quick check follows: clearly shows MATRICULA contract ID CPF possibly identifier personnel, latter come handy harmonization personnel module. Now, can begin creating set variables defined standard_dictionary vignette. often useful begin creating derived variables. four sets derived variables within dictionary: Industrial Standard Classification Occupation (ISCO) variables, .e. occupation_isconame, occupation_iscocode derived original occupation variables occupation_native, occupation_english. apply polyglotr::google_translate() function convert Portuguese named occupations English well use LabourR::classify_occupation() function classify occupations level-4 isco names. date variables (ref_date, start_date, end_date) often serial 5-digit format need standardized used preparing compensation variables time-variant. , create date variables: compensation variables .e. gross_salary_ppp, base_salary_ppp, net_salary_ppp derived local currency equivalents gross_salary_lcu, base_salary_lcu, net_salary_lcu. provide function called convert_constant_ppp() well macro_indicators dataset package perform transformations nominal variables (.e. _lcu) real equivalents (_ppp). contract type variable TIPO_CONTRATO needs reclassified according dictionary, contract_type. follows: Let’s data.table join contract_dict bra_hrmis Now derived variables contract module created, ready create rest variables finalize module. final data looks like:
code: raw_dictionary <-    tibble(raw_colnames_pt = colnames(govhr::bra_hrmis),          raw_colnames_eng = polyglotr::google_translate(colnames(bra_hrmis), "pt", "en"))  kable(raw_dictionary) ### first let us convert the data to a data.table object to speed up our computations  bra_hrmis <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis)  # Unique CPF per year cpf_summary <- bra_hrmis[, .(unique_cpf = uniqueN(CPF),                              nobs       = .N),                          by = ANO_PAGAMENTO]  # Unique Matricula per year mtr_summary <- bra_hrmis[, .(unique_mtr = uniqueN(MATRICULA),                              nobs       = .N),                           by = ANO_PAGAMENTO]  kable(cpf_summary) kable(mtr_summary) #----------------------------- # 2. Build occupation table (active + inactive) #-----------------------------  occup_df <- bra_hrmis[, c("CARREIRA", "CARGO")]  # distinct CARREIRA/CARGO/status occup_df <- unique(occup_df)  # Add translated vars occup_df[, occupation_native := tolower(CARREIRA)]  occup_df[, occupation_english := tolower(polyglotr::google_translate(text = occupation_native,                                                           source_language = "pt",                                                           target_language = "en"))] class_occup_df <- copy(occup_df)[,   .(id = .I, text = occupation_english) ]  class_occup_df <- classify_occupation(   class_occup_df,   isco_level = 4,   lang = "en",   num_leaves = 1 ) ## Warning in .maybe_warn_merge_dots(...): merge.data.table() received 1 unknown ## keyword argument which will be ignored: [on] ## Warning in .maybe_warn_merge_dots(...): merge.data.table() received 1 unknown ## keyword argument which will be ignored: [on] #----------------------------- # 4. Merge classification back into occup_df #----------------------------- occup_df[, id := .I]  # merge iscoGroup occup_df <- merge(   occup_df,   class_occup_df[, .(id = as.integer(id), iscoGroup)],   by = "id",   all.x = TRUE )  setnames(occup_df, "iscoGroup", "occupation_iscocode")  # merge ISCO descriptions occup_df <- merge(occup_df,                   isco[, c("unit", "description")] |> as.data.table(),                   by.x = "occupation_iscocode",                   by.y = "unit",                   all.x = TRUE)  setnames(occup_df, "description", "occupation_isconame")  #----------------------------- # 5. Bring classified occupations back to bra_hrmis (active only) #-----------------------------  ## we perform a left join with data.table syntax for speed as the merging into  ## the hrmis dataset could be computationally intensive  bra_hrmis <- occup_df[bra_hrmis, on = c("CARREIRA", "CARGO")] ### lets include the dates bra_hrmis[, ref_date := as.Date(paste(ANO_PAGAMENTO, MES_REFERENCIA, "01", sep = "-"))]  setnames(bra_hrmis, c("DATA_ADMISSAO", "DATA_APOSENTADORIA"), c("start_date", "end_date"), skip_absent = TRUE) bra_hrmis[, start_date := as.Date(as.integer(start_date), origin = "1899-12-30")] bra_hrmis[, end_date := as.Date(as.integer(end_date), origin = "1899-12-30")]   ### lets include the country code and admin identifier  bra_hrmis[, country_code := "BRA"] bra_hrmis[, country_name := "Brazil"] bra_hrmis[, adm1_name := "Alagoas"] bra_hrmis[, adm1_code := "AL"] ### lets convert the nominal compensation variables to real (_ppp) values # Step 1: Create the _lcu salary variables (in-place, no copy)  ### lets rename the raw variables here to their actual names setnames(bra_hrmis,           old = c("SALARIO_BASE", "SALARIO_BRUTO", "SALARIO_LIQUIDO", "ABONO_PERMANENCIA"),          new = c("base_salary_lcu", "gross_salary_lcu", "net_salary_lcu", "allowance_lcu"))   # Step 2: Identify all *_lcu columns to convert cols_to_convert <- grep("_lcu$", names(bra_hrmis), value = TRUE)  # Step 3: Apply PPP conversion using your convert_constant_ppp function pfw_df <-    macro_indicators |>   dplyr::filter(country_code == "BRA",                  year %in% as.integer(unique(bra_hrmis$ANO_PAGAMENTO))) |>   dplyr::select(all_of(c("country_code", "year", "cpi", "ppp")))   bra_hrmis[, (cols_to_convert) := lapply(.SD, as.numeric), .SDcols = cols_to_convert]   ### apply the convert_constant_ppp function to produce those estimates bra_hrmis <- convert_constant_ppp(data = bra_hrmis[, year := lubridate::year(ref_date)],                                   cols = cols_to_convert,                                   macro_indicators = macro_indicators)  ### while we are at this lets include the working hour variable as well bra_hrmis[, whours := as.numeric(JORNADA)] ### create a little dictionary mapping all the raw classes into a contract type in a data.table contract_dict <-    data.table(TIPO_CONTRATO = unique(bra_hrmis$TIPO_CONTRATO),              contract_type = c("short-term", "permanent", "permanent", "open-term",                                "short-term", "inactive", "retired"))  kable(contract_dict) bra_hrmis <- contract_dict[bra_hrmis, on = "TIPO_CONTRATO"] setnames(bra_hrmis,          old = c("MATRICULA", "CPF", "ORGAO", "CLASSE", "NIVEL"),          new = c("contract_id", "personnel_id", "est_id", "paygrade", "seniority"))   ### now let us select the final set of dictionary variables to complete the module ### lets use dplyr::select() function since this will not add any computational time bra_hrmis_contract <-    bra_hrmis |>   dplyr::select(     contract_id, personnel_id, est_id,     ends_with("_date"),     contains("_salary_"),     contract_type,      starts_with("occupation_"),     country_code, country_name,     adm1_name, adm1_code,     whours, paygrade, seniority   )

what: Generate Standard HR Analytics Report — generate_hr_report
title: Generate Standard HR Analytics Report — generate_hr_report
text: Produces comprehensive HTML analytics report harmonized HR data using Quarto template. report includes descriptive statistics, visualizations, optional quality control diagnostics across Contract, Personnel, Establishment modules.

title: Generate Standard HR Analytics Report — generate_hr_report
code: generate_hr_report(   contract_dt,   personnel_dt,   est_dt,   country_code,   output = "hr_report.html" )

title: Generate Standard HR Analytics Report — generate_hr_report
text: contract_dt data.table containing Contract module data harmonized column names according harmonization_dict. include columns contract_id, personnel_id, est_id, ref_date, salary fields, occupation information. personnel_dt data.table containing Personnel module data harmonized column names. include personnel_id demographic information. est_dt data.table containing Establishment module data harmonized column names. include est_id establishment characteristics. country_code reference country code. Must specified three-letter, World Bank standard (e.g., BRA Brazil). output Character string specifying output file name. Defaults "hr_report.html". file created current working directory.

title: Generate Standard HR Analytics Report — generate_hr_report
text: HR report, HTML.

title: Generate Standard HR Analytics Report — generate_hr_report
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Generate HR analytics report for Brazilian HRMIS data generate_hr_report(   contract_dt = bra_hrmis_contract,   personnel_dt = bra_hrmis_personnel,   est_dt = bra_hrmis_est,   country_code = "BRA",   output = "brazil_hr_report.html" ) } # }
